dedupe_keys.name: great britain accessibility indicators 2023 ai23 public transport cycling and walking

description: The Great Britain Accessibility Indicators 2023 (AI23) provide ready-to-use measures of how easily people can reach key services by public transport, bicycle and on foot. For about 42,000 small areas (LSOAs in England and Wales and Data Zones in Scotland) they report cumulative counts of employment, GP practices, hospitals, pharmacies, parks, primary and secondary schools, supermarkets and main and sub urban centres within 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes, with public transport times for a 7 a.m. and a 9 p.m. departure. It updates and extends the Public Transport Accessibility Indicators 2022 (PTAI22), described in Scientific Data, and was produced by J. Rafael Verduzco Torres and David McArthur (version 2023.1, February 2024), with a data descriptor preprint. Coverage is national (Great Britain). The data are free under the Open Government Licence 3.0 and available to download from Zenodo as one ZIP archive (about 143 MB). Caveats: the indicators are modelled from timetables and networks for 2023 and use 2011 area codes. They support the assessment of service accessibility, the equity effects of transport disruption and capacity planning of public transport. They complement the DfT journey time statistics and are related to the MOBILITY MAPS public transport accessibility for Germany.
